title: Normalized invocation pathway mart for per-route SLA & cost attribution
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Purpose: Build a normalized invocation-pathways mart that surfaces per-route and per-tenant SLA (p99/p95 latency) and per-invocation cost attribution while preserving query performance for common console dashboards. Scope: define canonical grain, dimension sets, transformation rules to collapse noisy low-level events into ordered invocation sequences, handle retries/forks, and emit a compact fact table plus lightweight dimension tables. Key deliverables: 1) canonical schema and ER diagram, 2) ETL transforms for sessionized invocation sequences, 3) materialized summary tables for p95/p99 and cost factors, 4) migration and backfill plan, 5) tests & dashboards. Grain: one row per invocation-pathway-step (ordered step index) with stable invocation_id and pathway_id. Non-goals: full raw-event retention or replacing existing sessionized pipelines during initial rollout.
data_model_notes: Grain: invocation_step (invocation_id, pathway_id, step_index); Fact columns: event_ts, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, route_id, workspace_id, cost_estimate_cents, outcome_code; Dimensions: route_meta(route_id, name, product_area), workspace_meta(workspace_id, tier, billing_entity), model_catalog(model_variant, family, quantized_flag). Use SCD2 for route_meta and workspace_meta. Partitioning: partition fact by date(event_ts) and cluster by workspace_id, route_id. Retention: raw source events 90d, mart 540d. Backfill window strategy: backfill last 180d for initial analytics.
transformation_steps: 1) Ingest event stream and normalize keys (client_request_id -> invocation_id canonicalization). 2) Window events into invocation by invocation_id with tight ordering and dedupe using event_ts + sequence_hash. 3) Collapse retry/fork events: keep FIRST successful or LAST failed semantics configurable by config flag. 4) Compute step-level metrics (latency_ms, token deltas, model variant selection). 5) Emit pathway-level aggregates: total_latency, total_cost_estimate, step_count, p95/p99 markers. 6) Populate materialized summary tables and maintain incremental snapshots for SLA rollup and cost attribution.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Schema reviewed and approved by analytics and SRE. 2) Incremental transform runs under target latency (< 15m for daily window). 3) Sampled queries for p95/p99 and per-route cost return within 2s for common filters. 4) Automated tests for dedupe/windowing with synthetic retry/fork scenarios. 5) Backfill completes for 180d sample without data loss and with row counts matching source event counts for canonical invocations.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy transforms to staging, run end-to-end validation with synthetic workloads and compare against golden query results. Phase 2: run side-by-side in prod pipeline writing to _preview tables for 7 days; validate dashboards and SLO bookkeeping. Phase 3: switch dashboards to mart tables and begin 180d backfill to canonical table; monitor query perf and cost. Phase 4: enable 540d retention and mark old session tables as read-only before deprecation warning cycle.
migration_risks: - Risk: mis-canonicalization of invocation_id across SDK versions -> mitigation: include ingestion-time fingerprint and map table; run compatibility audit. - Risk: backfill cost spikes -> mitigation: limit parallelism and use throttled workers + cost budget alerting. - Risk: SCD2 bloat for workspace_meta -> mitigation: compact historical changes monthly and use dimension surrogate keys.
perf_considerations: Materialize common aggregates (per-route p95/p99/day, per-tenant cost/day). Use incremental materialized views with delta-processing. Leverage compact integer surrogate keys for joins. Estimate final mart size: ~120M rows/month before aggregation; projected queries: top 50 dashboards for console will hit aggregates not raw mart. Benchmark: expected 3x speedup vs raw-event ad-hoc joins for p95 queries.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for windowing and dedupe, integration tests with sample event traces, SLO regression tests comparing output to baseline for a 30-day sample, data quality checks: null-rate thresholds, row-count reconciliation, distinct invocation counts. Create CI job that runs quick smoke backfill and asserts invariants.
monitoring_and_alerting: Setup ingestion lag dashboards, backfill progress gauge, daily reconciliation jobs to compare invocation counts vs source, anomaly alert for sudden change in p95/p99 or cost per-invocation > 30% day-over-day. Add tracing tags for pipeline runs for fast root cause.
